body: @knutwannheden Hm, I've just tried to modify the `embedded.html` in the qute extension and it renders correctly the value `/` which is the default value for `quarkus.http.root-path`.

Hmm... I have to test this again. Possibly I ran my test in an multi-module Maven project where the Quarkus extension was part of the same Maven reactor build as the test project. Could that be a problem?

> Hmm... I have to test this again. Possibly I ran my test in an multi-module Maven project where the Quarkus extension was part of the same Maven reactor build as the test project. Could that be a problem?

I have no idea :-). Anyway, let me know if it turns out to be a multi-module bug.

Yes, you are right: The default value is properly found and returned. However, what doesn't work is that if I modify the default (e.g. using `application.properties`) then this value is not found and returned. As a result my extension's card will end up using the HTTP root `/` rather than e.g. `/foo`.

> Yes, you are right: The default value is properly found and returned. However, what doesn't work is that if I modify the default (e.g. using `application.properties`) then this value is not found and returned. As a result my extension's card will end up using the HTTP root `/` rather than e.g. `/foo`.

You're right. I can confirm that the default value is used.

So the config namespace resolver is using `ConfigProvider.getConfig().getOptionalValue()` which is probably wrong? I can see that the config editor page is built on top of `List<ConfigDescriptionBuildItem>`. Maybe we should switch to these build items as well? @radcortez @phillip-kruger WDYT?

Hum, if you see multiple `SmallRyeConfig` instances being created it means that the lookup was done on the wrong classloader so a new one is created to the current classloader. That means that the configuration may differ completely.

The`ConfigDescriptionBuildItem` does not carry the config value resolution. Just metadata like the config description that the regular `Config` instance does not have.

Let me have a look into it.
@radcortez Yes, that was also my thinking. And like I said, the instance being used here is created at the point when the dev console is first accessed.

> The`ConfigDescriptionBuildItem` does not carry the config value resolution.

Hmm, you're right. The value is populated lazily, when the table of config editor is loaded and it also uses `ConfigProvider.getConfig()`. The difference is that we register the value resolver in a `io.quarkus.vertx.http.deployment.devmode.console.DevConsoleProcessor` method, i.e. using a different TCCL. I'll try to fix it.

issue.title: Dev UI - fix config namespace resolver
issue.body:
- use the function stored in the DevConsoleRecorder to make sure the
config is obtained using the correct TCCL
- resolves #21691
